why: The student turns the whole switch into an equivalent else-if chain, and correctly joins the fall-through labels case 2 and case 3 with ||; this links switch to the if-else chain, but 'elif' is not Java syntax, so it is a relational answer with an error.

concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: The chain structure is right and the final else catches the default case, but Java needs 'else if', not 'elif'.
The answer says nothing about the plain if on its own.
Uses || to join two comparisons into one condition that covers the grouped case labels.
The answer makes no claim about statements.
The assignments are copied from the code without any reasoning about them.
The answer says nothing about evaluation order.
It matches each case to an == test on value, merges the fall-through labels and maps default to else, but the code would not compile because of 'elif'.
